question.text: Why can a 5-server cluster keep working with 2 servers down while a 4-server cluster can only lose 1? Behind that: why must the decision rule be "more than half of all servers"?
question.result_stated: Yes, in words, at line 5: "For 5 servers, more than half is 3, so 5 − 3 = 2 servers can fail. For 4 servers, more than half is also 3, so only 4 − 3 = 1 server can fail."

reply.motive: Reason to care about the question: the split-brain table and line 34, "Both groups decide, and the copies now disagree for good." Reason for the approach: line 25, "A sees the same silence in both cases, so A cannot know which case is true", which explains why survivors cannot simply go on. Line 70 adds a practical payoff: "That is why clusters usually have an odd number of servers."
reply.close: Yes. Line 74: "Both clusters need 3 servers to decide a change, because 3 is the smallest group that must share a server with every other group. 5 servers have 2 to spare. 4 servers have only 1." This states the general overlap argument in words, though only loosely.
reply.recap: A cluster needs a majority of all its servers to agree, so that any two deciding groups share a server that blocks conflicting decisions; 4 and 5 servers both need 3, so 5 has one more server to spare.
reply.strongest: Lines 25-34: the indistinguishable-silence point leads straight into the partition table, which shows split brain concretely.
reply.weakest: Line 42: the switch from 4 to 5 servers leaves out the setup in which C first accepted x = 1.
suggestions: Before line 42, add one sentence such as "Suppose A, B, C have already accepted x = 1 for change 7, and D, E now receive x = 2."
After the 5-server overlap example at line 40, add the general sentence: two groups that each hold more than half of n servers together count more than n, so they must share a server.
Mention once at line 17 why a server accepts only one change per position (so that a shared server can block a conflict), or point ahead to line 42.
